kaigo-language-session-11-notes.heading: Distinguish sequence from starting conditions
paragraphs: “B after A” describes sequence, whereas “do not use until confirmed” sets a condition for action. Completing an earlier task does not establish that intervening checks or consent are complete.

For personal belongings, distinguish permission to move particular items from where their location will be checked afterward. Consent to move magazines is not permission to move photographs or every belonging.

The empty training-wheelchair memo teaches responsibilities for checking inspection records and moving equipment, not transfers or repairs. The evacuation-drill reception memo likewise is not a complete real-fire procedure.
The next three documents were created for learning. Mark responsible people, prerequisites and unfinished tasks, and check that you have not added unstated actions or permissions.

“Nakereba narimasen” means an action is necessary or obligatory; “te wa ikemasen” prohibits it. “You must check the date before submission” requires a date check, not forbids one. Read sentence endings and distinguish required from prohibited actions.

kaigo-reading-new-252.heading: Read consent scope for belongings
paragraphs:
Personal-belongings memo
Before arranging the shelf, explain items to move and where they will be returned.
Today the person agreed only to magazines on another shelf, not moving photographs.
Afterward, check the magazines’ location with the person. No completion is recorded.
Explain both items and return location before work. Today’s consent covers only magazines; photographs are not wanted moved. Distinguish general explanation from the specific consent scope.
The location check is planned after work. Without a completion record, neither arranging nor checking can be reported as finished.

kaigo-reading-new-253.heading: Read prerequisites for empty-wheelchair training
paragraphs:
Training-wheelchair management memo
Before training: The responsible worker checks inspection records. Do not use until confirmed.
Movement plan: After checking, move the empty wheelchair to the display area. No person will ride.
Instruction: The trainer will separately explain brake and tire inspection.
Current state: Record checking is not complete.
Use is conditional on the responsible worker confirming inspection records, which remains incomplete. Do not reinterpret this as inspected or already moved.
The planned move is an empty display wheelchair, without a person aboard. The trainer separately explains brakes and tires; do not infer and perform operations from this memo.

kaigo-reading-new-254.heading: Read drill reception order
paragraphs:
Evacuation-drill reception memo (practice)
A: Receive the list and tell the responsible worker it was received.
B: After A, wait for the drill-start announcement.
C: After the announcement, record numbers at the assembly-point reception.
This practices reception. In a real fire, follow facility emergency procedures.
After A’s receipt and notification, B waits for the announcement. C records numbers afterward, not immediately on receiving the list.
This practices drill reception, not all firefighting or evacuation-assistance procedures. In real fires, follow facility emergency procedures and necessary instructions.

kaigo-language-session-11-terms.heading: Document vocabulary reference
paragraphs: This is a reference list. Choose words needed for today’s documents rather than memorizing all at once.
条件（じょうけん） — Condition: something that must be met before starting or proceeding, distinct from order alone.
手順（てじゅん） — Procedure: what to do and in which order.
同意（どうい） — Consent: accepting specific explained content, not necessarily another task.
私物（しぶつ） — Belongings: personal items; confirm the scope of arrangement or movement with the person.
点検（てんけん） — Inspection: checking equipment condition. Distinguish reviewing a record from performing inspection.
受領（じゅりょう） — Receipt: receiving supplied items or documents.
開始放送（かいしほうそう） — Start announcement: a broadcast announcing the start of a drill or similar activity.
完了（かんりょう） — Completion: planned work has ended; a plan alone is not completion.

kaigo-language-session-12-notes.heading: Separate preparation, explanation, response and implementation
paragraphs: Preparing items, hearing explanations, choosing and carrying out an activity or assistance are separate events. Plans or supplies alone do not establish consent or completed support.
Activity preparation begins by asking participation wishes. Choose cards with those wishing to participate and proceed to later checks. Finished selection is not activity commencement.

These records do not specify individual water temperatures, fluid amounts, swallowing or posture instructions or rest lengths. Do not fill missing conditions with general numbers or improvised methods. Check condition and the current plan for actual support.
Read completed acts such as “explained” or “started” separately from future “planned” or “will check.” Even with times, determine whether the document is a schedule or performance record.

kaigo-reading-new-255.heading: From participation wishes to card preparation
paragraphs:
Activity-preparation memo
Ask participation wishes before starting.
Choose cards with willing participants, then check the selected count.
Finally give the starting time and explain that they may tell staff if they want to stop.
Card selection alone must not be recorded as activity started.
Ask wishes, select with willing participants, check count and then give start time. Also explain the option to tell staff they want to stop midway.
Finished card selection does not establish the activity started. Asking wishes and confirming actual participation or commencement remain separate.

kaigo-reading-new-256.heading: Prepared towels and outstanding checks
paragraphs:
Bathing-plan handoff
Morning: The person heard the afternoon bathing plan but wants to answer later about participation.
Preparation: Towels are ready. The responsible worker will check the environment and current condition.
Handoff: Discuss the day’s response after wishes and check results are known.
The morning explanation and towel preparation are complete. The person deferred answering, rather than deciding to bathe.
Environment and current condition checks remain ahead. Since the response follows wishes and check results, towels alone cannot establish all bathing conditions.

kaigo-reading-new-257.heading: Meal start and unknown outcomes
paragraphs:
Mealtime record
11:20: Staff explained the menu; the person asked one dish name again.
11:25: After the question was answered, eating began.
12:05: A post-meal preference check is planned. Intake and current condition are absent.
This record alone establishes neither full intake nor completed post-meal support.
At 11:20 came explanation and the repeated question; after an answer, eating began at 11:25. Preserve explanation, question, answer and start order.
12:05 is a planned preference check. Without intake or current condition, full eating or completed post-meal support cannot be established.

kaigo-language-session-12-terms.heading: Document vocabulary reference
paragraphs: This is a reference list. Choose words needed for today’s documents rather than memorizing all at once.
準備（じゅんび） — Preparation: arranging supplies or conditions needed for upcoming action.
用意済み（よういずみ） — Prepared: the task of preparing necessary items is complete.
参加（さんか） — Participation: joining an activity, not simply hearing an explanation.
献立（こんだて） — Menu: the combination of dishes served in a meal.
聞き直す（ききなおす） — Ask again: request repetition or clarification of something not understood.
予定（よてい） — Plan: intended future time or content.
実施（じっし） — Implementation: actually carrying out a plan.
未記載（みきさい） — Not recorded: information is absent from the document or field, not proof nothing happened.

kaigo-language-session-13-notes.heading: Check notice audience, period, exceptions and purpose
paragraphs: For notices, first identify audience, valid period and changed location. Check consultation contacts for accessibility difficulties and information in separate guides. Do not expand a limited notice into rules for everyone or every item.
Distinguish contact deadlines from item-delivery deadlines. A family inquiry about photo displays does not establish the person wants display too. Confirm items and personal wishes specifically.
Numbered distribution steps for handwashing materials differ from handwashing movements. Read title and purpose, then identify who checks the version, marks words and explains.
The next three notices are fictional learning situations. Their dates and contacts are not real facility rules; check your organization’s current guidance for actual action.

kaigo-reading-new-258.heading: Reception-change period and separate information
paragraphs:
Visitor notice (fictional facility)
Reception change: From November 6 through 9, visiting reception is at the east entrance. Usual reception resumes November 10.
Contact: If the east entrance is difficult to use, consult reception before visiting.
Telephone: Call during opening hours, specified in a separate guide.
East-entrance reception applies November 6–9 and usual reception from the 10th. Those with difficulty should consult before visiting. Preserve audience and period.
Exact phone hours are not in this notice; consult the separate guide. Do not invent typical opening times.

kaigo-reading-new-259.heading: Photo-display contact deadline and personal wishes
paragraphs:
Exhibition-preparation notice
Families: If you have photographs to display, contact the responsible worker by October 2. Bring photos after receiving confirmation.
Staff: Ask the person’s display wishes too; family contact alone must not decide display.
This concerns photo display. Check other belongings’ rules separately.
October 2 is the deadline to contact the responsible worker about photographs. Bringing them follows confirmation; do not change the contact deadline into a delivery deadline.
Ask the person’s wishes too rather than deciding from family contact alone. Check non-photo belongings separately.

kaigo-reading-new-260.heading: Distribution procedure versus handwashing movements
paragraphs:
Handwashing-training material distribution memo
1. The responsible worker checks the current version.
2. After confirmation, distribute materials to participants.
3. Participants mark unfamiliar words; the trainer explains.
No handwashing movements are specified here. Practice follows confirmed materials and instruction.
The responsible worker checks the version, participants receive materials and mark unfamiliar words, and the trainer explains. Distribution follows version confirmation.

The three numbers describe distribution responsibilities, not three washing movements. Practice follows confirmed materials and instruction; do not invent movements or disinfection conditions from this text.

kaigo-language-session-13-terms.heading: Document vocabulary reference
paragraphs: This is a reference list. Choose words needed for today’s documents rather than memorizing all at once.
掲示（けいじ） — Posting: displaying guidance visibly to inform people.
来訪（らいほう） — Visit: someone coming to a facility or similar place.
受付（うけつけ） — Reception: the desk or work handling visitors’ procedures or inquiries.
期限（きげん） — Deadline: the last point by which an action must be completed; check which action.
持参（じさん） — Bringing: personally bringing an item, unlike contact alone.
版（はん） — Version: distinguishes document content or revisions; check the current version.
配布（はいふ） — Distribution: giving materials to the necessary people.
印を付ける（しるしをつける） — Mark: add an indicator identifying a noticed area.

kaigo-language-session-14-notes.heading: Read tables by date, meal and responsibility
paragraphs: Read menus row by row using both date and mealtime, distinguishing staple, side-dish and dessert columns. Nashi written なし (none) and 梨 (pear) sound alike but differ according to spelling and column.
Event plans distinguish planned from actual counts and preparing staff from people choosing participation methods. A list alone does not establish everyone accepted the same role.
When conditions such as location change, identify changed and unchanged points and ask wishes again. Creating a change notice differs from completing family notification.
These are learning schedules. Explain one changed, unchanged and pending point from each. Do not summarize planned entries as everything confirmed.

kaigo-reading-new-261.heading: Match date and meal columns and distinguish homophones
paragraphs:
Menu-check memo (planned)
September 12, lunch: staple—barley rice; side—steamed fish; dessert—apple.
September 12, dinner: staple—rice; side—tofu with sauce; dessert—なし (none).
September 13, lunch: staple—bread; side—vegetable soup; dessert—梨 (pear).
Here なし means no dessert and 梨 is fruit. Record actual serving separately.
September 12 lunch has steamed fish as side; September 13 lunch has bread as staple. Dinner’s なし on the 12th means no dessert, while lunch’s 梨 on the 13th means pear.
This is a planned menu. Dish names alone do not establish actual serving or eating. Separate performed service from intake checks.

kaigo-reading-new-262.heading: Event counts, responsibilities and choices
paragraphs:
Reading-aloud gathering plan
Date/time: April 18, 14:10–14:50. Place: library corner.
Planned: 8 people receiving care and 2 staff. Record actual attendance afterward.
Roles: A prepares books; B discusses seats with those wanting them.
People may choose reading, listening or not attending. Do not assign roles from the list alone.
April 18, 14:10–14:50 in the library corner is planned. Eight people and two staff total ten, but actual attendance is recorded afterward.
A prepares books and B discusses requested seating. Since the person may read, listen or decline, the list alone does not assign everyone a reading role.

kaigo-reading-new-263.heading: Location change and outstanding contact
paragraphs:
Craft-exchange change notice
Location changed from courtyard to indoor salon. Start remains 15:20.
A: Notify families about the location.
B: Ask whether people still wish to participate after the change.
C: Prepare display cards. Family notification is not finished.
The location changed to the indoor salon from the courtyard. Start time remains 15:20; do not add a time change.
A handles family contact, B checks renewed participation wishes, C prepares cards. Family contact is unfinished; the written change is not completed notification.

kaigo-language-session-14-terms.heading: Document vocabulary reference
paragraphs: This is a reference list. Choose words needed for today’s documents rather than memorizing all at once.
主食（しゅしょく） — Staple: a meal’s central food category, such as rice or bread; match the column.
副食（ふくしょく） — Side dish: food eaten with staples; do not confuse its column with staples.
梨（なし） — Pear: fruit, distinguished in writing from なし meaning none.
参加予定（さんかよてい） — Planned participation: anticipated attendance, not actual confirmation.
担当（たんとう） — Responsibility: an assigned task or check, or the person assigned.
変更（へんこう） — Change: alteration of some content; also check what stays unchanged.
行事（ぎょうじ） — Event: a planned gathering or similar occasion.
希望（きぼう） — Wish: what the person wants to do or have done.

kaigo-language-session-15-notes.heading: Dates across midnight, discovery, causes and responses
paragraphs: Read night-shift dates and times together. The next day’s midnight hour follows the previous day’s 22:00 hour. Do not sort by numerical size alone; identify the date change and calculate elapsed time.
Finding damage differs from knowing who caused it or how. Separate observed condition from causal judgment and report unknown causes as unknown.
Contacting, entering a field or requesting inspection or replacement does not prove the recipient read, agreed or completed action. Check recipient and outcome separately.
These fictional business records teach reading. Distinguish confirmed facts, unknown causes and requests with unconfirmed results. Check that blame has not been assigned without evidence.

“Number within a period” expresses frequency. Updating materials once every three weeks differs from weekly. Start time, duration and frequency are separate facts. This example concerns document updates, not intervals for rounds or condition checks.

kaigo-reading-new-264.heading: Scheduled versus actual completion times
paragraphs:
Day-shift work checklist
09:40 (planned): Sort materials. Actual finish 09:55.
10:10 (planned): Check notices. No start record yet.
12:10–12:40 (planned): Break. Record any change.
14:30 (planned): Report check results to the responsible worker, identifying unconfirmed items as unconfirmed.
Material sorting actually ended 09:55 against the 09:40 plan. The planned 10:10 notice check lacks a start record, so inspection cannot be treated as already done.
The 12:10–12:40 break is 30 minutes planned. 14:30 is a planned report, not proof all items are complete. Unknowns remain unknown in the report.

kaigo-reading-new-265.heading: Next-day midnight and unchecked receipt
paragraphs:
Night-shift contact memo
October 22, 22:50: Received a change to next morning’s visit plan.
October 23, 00:20: Entered the change in the handoff field.
October 23, 06:15 (planned): Explain to day staff.
Entry is complete, but whether day staff read it is unconfirmed.
October 22 at 22:50 to October 23 at 00:20 is 1 hour 30 minutes. The latter follows the date change, so it is not earlier.
Entry is complete, but day-staff reading is unknown. The 06:15 explanation is planned; entry alone is not completed explanation.

kaigo-reading-new-266.heading: Damage discovery versus unknown cause and replacement
paragraphs:
Equipment-damage report
Discovery: At 08:35 in the lounge, staff found a cracked desk-clock cover.
Prior circumstances: Previous user and how it cracked are unknown.
Response: Reported and requested inspection and replacement from the responsible worker. No completion notice yet.
Add only confirmed facts.
The discovered fact is a cracked cover at 08:35 in the lounge. Prior user and mechanism are unknown; do not invent a drop, cause or blame.
Reporting and requests occurred, but completion has not been notified. Add only confirmed facts, without assuming replacement.

kaigo-language-session-15-terms.heading: Document vocabulary reference
paragraphs: This is a reference list. Choose words needed for today’s documents rather than memorizing all at once.
日勤（にっきん） — Day shift: work mainly in daytime; check exact times at the workplace or schedule.
夜勤（やきん） — Night shift: work including night; read dates and times together across midnight.
翌朝（よくあさ） — Next morning: the morning of the following day.
記入（きにゅう） — Entry: writing needed information in document fields.
発見（はっけん） — Discovery: noticing a previously unnoticed condition or event.
破損（はそん） — Damage: an item breaking, for example with a cracked part.
原因（げんいん） — Cause: what led to a state or event; do not fill unknowns with guesses.
追記（ついき） — Additional entry: adding information later to an existing record.

kaigo-language-session-16-notes.heading: Hand over individual exceptions and changed plans
paragraphs: Match transport times and methods to each person or code. Do not generalize one exception to everyone; hand over pending facts in that person’s field. R1–R3 here are fictional codes.

Gathering and departure are separate times. In changes, identify old and new before calculating intervals. A corrected notice does not automatically prove the person heard, understood or agreed to new times.
“It is quiet now” expresses the person’s feeling at that moment. Do not invalidate earlier concerns or infer that a cause was removed or sleep lasted until morning.
These learning records practice handoff reading. Match words, hearing times and reporting times without adding causes or later conditions absent from the text.

kaigo-reading-new-267.heading: Match return times and methods by code
paragraphs:
Transport-plan handoff (fictional codes)
Morning planned arrivals: R1, R2, R3—three people.
Afternoon return: R1 at 14:40 by facility vehicle; R2 at 15:10 with family.
R3’s time and method are being checked. Do not say everyone uses the same vehicle.
Record actual arrival and return separately.
Three arrivals are planned. R1 returns at 14:40 by facility vehicle and R2 at 15:10 with family. Do not apply one method to everyone.
R3’s return time and method are being checked. Plans do not establish actual arrival or return; check results separately. Do not connect fictional codes to real people’s abilities or histories.

kaigo-reading-new-268.heading: New gathering/departure and explanation status
paragraphs:
Outing-plan change
Old: Tomorrow gather 09:05, depart 09:15.
New: Tomorrow gather 09:35, depart 09:50. Destination and accompanying staff unchanged.
Check: The responsible worker will explain new times. Completed explanation is unconfirmed.
Pick-up method is not stated.
Use new gathering 09:35 and departure 09:50, a 15-minute gap. Do not confuse gathering with departure or keep using old 09:05/09:15 times.
Destination and accompanying staff are unchanged but unnamed. Explanation completion is unknown and pick-up method unstated. Document changes do not establish heard or agreed information.

kaigo-reading-new-269.heading: Two timed statements and reporting
paragraphs:
Night contact record
21:40: The person said, “The corridor noise bothers me.” Cause unknown.
22:05: When asked, the person said, “It is quiet now.”
22:10: Both timed statements and unknown cause reported to the responsible worker.
Subsequent sleep is not recorded.
At 21:40 noise bothered the person; at 22:05 it was quiet. Preserve feelings at both times rather than erase the earlier concern.
At 22:10 both accounts and unknown cause were reported. Subsequent sleep is absent, so neither resolved cause nor a good night’s sleep is established. This is not diagnosis or treatment instruction.

kaigo-language-session-16-terms.heading: Document vocabulary reference
paragraphs: This is a reference list. Choose words needed for today’s documents rather than memorizing all at once.
送迎（そうげい） — Transport: taking people to and from places.
到着（とうちゃく） — Arrival: reaching the intended place.
帰宅（きたく） — Returning home: going back to one’s residence.
集合（しゅうごう） — Gathering: assembling at an agreed place, distinct from departure.
出発（しゅっぱつ） — Departure: leaving toward a destination.
確認中（かくにんちゅう） — Under checking: information is being checked, not finalized.
申し送り（もうしおくり） — Handoff: passing information needed for support to the next worker or similar recipient.
睡眠（すいみん） — Sleep: sleeping; a quietness statement alone does not establish sleep outcomes.

kaigo-gap-hand-legend.heading: Read commonly missed hand-area diagrams correctly
paragraphs: A two-shade hand diagram distinguishes commonly missed from especially commonly missed areas. Shades are cautions, not measured microorganism counts or percentages of cleanliness.
Palms and backs are different surfaces. One looking washed does not establish coverage of finger webs, fingertips and nails, thumbs and their bases, or wrists. Review both hands and relevant areas.
Uncolored areas are not guaranteed clean. Check area names and surfaces; neither lighter shading nor no color authorizes omission.

This unit teaches the legend and commonly missed areas. Infection precautions require hand hygiene at appropriate times and with appropriate methods. With visible dirt, check washing using water and soap; actual performance follows facility training and product instructions.

[Learning comparison] A learner thinks a clean-looking palm removes other checks. Do not infer the whole from one part; check backs, webs, fingertips, thumbs, wrists and other required areas. The diagram cannot determine a disinfection percentage.

155.title: Read procedure conditions and consent scope
objectives: Explain sequence, action conditions and accepted scope separately.
Distinguish empty-equipment training from actual assistance and drill roles from emergency response.
155.context: Read conditions, timing, responsibilities and the confirmed scope in project-created learning documents. Do not turn fictional times or rules into actual care instructions.
155.artCaption: Staff check procedures and conditions. The image does not show stair mobility or evacuation assistance methods.

156.title: Distinguish preparation from actual results
objectives: Separate preparation, explanation, choice, performance and results by their timing.
Do not invent absent care conditions or intake; identify needed checks.
156.context: Read conditions, timing, responsibilities and the confirmed scope in project-created learning documents. Do not turn fictional times or rules into actual care instructions.
156.artCaption: Discuss prepared supplies and outstanding checks. Supplies alone do not establish completed help.

157.title: Check notice periods, audience and purpose
objectives: Organize audience, period, contact deadlines and delivery conditions.
Do not turn distribution steps into handwashing movements.
157.context: Read conditions, timing, responsibilities and the confirmed scope in project-created learning documents. Do not turn fictional times or rules into actual care instructions.
157.artCaption: Compare two notices and check audience and validity before conveying them.

158.title: Read menus and event plans row by row
objectives: Match date, meal and column; distinguish なし and 梨 through context.
Distinguish planned counts, choices, changes and unfinished contact.
158.context: Read conditions, timing, responsibilities and the confirmed scope in project-created learning documents. Do not turn fictional times or rules into actual care instructions.
158.artCaption: Staff check written information. Use the relevant text row for actual menu and roles.

159.title: Read cross-date records and unknown causes
objectives: Order times across dates and explain elapsed time.
Report discovery separately from cause and requests separately from completion.
159.context: Read conditions, timing, responsibilities and the confirmed scope in project-created learning documents. Do not turn fictional times or rules into actual care instructions.
159.artCaption: Read night records with both dates and times. Do not move old results into new fields.

160.title: Hand over exceptions and revised plans accurately
objectives: Match code-specific transport and old/new gathering and departure times.
Preserve timed personal statements without adding absent causes or sleep outcomes.
160.context: Read conditions, timing, responsibilities and the confirmed scope in project-created learning documents. Do not turn fictional times or rules into actual care instructions.
160.artCaption: Distinguish recording from confirmed receipt. This image does not show transport or sleep results.

161.title: Check hand-hygiene legends and areas
objectives: Explain shades as warnings about missed areas.
Check both surfaces and required sites without inferring cleanliness percentages.
161.context: Read a color-coded hand legend and identify commonly missed sites. Shading does not measure actual contamination or microbial removal.
161.artCaption: Handwashing with water and soap is shown, not the two-color legend or confirmation of all stages.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-252.prompt: Which correctly reads consent and task status?
options: Consent permits moving magazines and photos.
Explain items now but return locations only afterward.
The magazine-location check is recorded complete.
Explain items and return locations first; today’s consent is magazines only, with no completion recorded.
rationales: Photos are not wanted moved; this expands scope.
Return location also belongs in the advance explanation.
The later check is planned, not completed.
This separates prior explanation, specific consent and absent completion.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-252.reading:
Personal-belongings memo
Before arranging the shelf, explain items to move and where they will be returned.
Today the person agreed only to magazines on another shelf, not moving photographs.
Afterward, check the magazines’ location with the person. No completion is recorded.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-253.prompt: What is known about the training wheelchair?
options: Records checked and an occupant moved to display.
Checking unfinished, but all inspection methods are in this memo.
Checking unfinished; an empty chair will move afterward, with inspection instruction separately.
No occupant means no record-check condition.
rationales: Both unfinished checking and the no-occupant condition are changed.
The trainer explains methods separately; no full procedure is here.
This preserves current status, conditional plan and empty-chair condition.
Even empty equipment must not be used before confirmation.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-253.reading:
Training-wheelchair management memo
Before training: The responsible worker checks inspection records. Do not use until confirmed.
Movement plan: After checking, move the empty wheelchair to the display area. No person will ride.
Instruction: The trainer will separately explain brake and tire inspection.
Current state: Record checking is not complete.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-254.prompt: Which order and scope match drill reception?
options: Receive and notify, wait for announcement, then record numbers; reception practice only.
Receive the list, immediately count, then await announcement.
Wait first and count before receiving the list.
A–C describe transfer techniques.
rationales: This preserves A–B–C and practice scope.
Counts follow announcement; waiting is omitted here.
B follows completion of A, not first.
These are list, announcement and attendance tasks, not transfers.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-254.reading:
Evacuation-drill reception memo (practice)
A: Receive the list and tell the responsible worker it was received.
B: After A, wait for the drill-start announcement.
C: After the announcement, record numbers at the assembly-point reception.
This practices reception. In a real fire, follow facility emergency procedures.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-255.prompt: Which preparation order and recording scope are appropriate?
options: Staff select all cards, start and then ask wishes.
Card selection proves the activity started.
Determine card counts without checking participation choice.
Ask wishes, choose with willing people, check count and start time; selection alone is not commencement.
rationales: Wishes come before selection and starting.
Selection and actual start are explicitly distinct.
Count follows selection with willing participants, not omitted wishes.
This retains conditions and order, including explaining the option to stop.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-255.reading:
Activity-preparation memo
Ask participation wishes before starting.
Choose cards with willing participants, then check the selected count.
Finally give the starting time and explain that they may tell staff if they want to stop.
Card selection alone must not be recorded as activity started.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-256.prompt: Which combines prepared and outstanding bathing items?
options: Towels, consent and safe environment all confirmed.
Towels ready; response, environment and current-condition checks outstanding.
Bathing refused and towels unprepared.
Hearing the plan counts as completed bathing.
rationales: Towels do not establish consent or environment checks.
This preserves deferred response and future responsible-worker checks.
Deferral is not refusal; towels are prepared.
Explanation differs from participation decision or actual bathing.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-256.reading:
Bathing-plan handoff
Morning: The person heard the afternoon bathing plan but wants to answer later about participation.
Preparation: Towels are ready. The responsible worker will check the environment and current condition.
Handoff: Discuss the day’s response after wishes and check results are known.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-257.prompt: Which separates mealtime facts, plans and absent information?
options: 11:20 explanation/question, 11:25 start after answer; 12:05 preference check planned, intake unstated.
Eating 11:20, first explanation 11:25.
12:05 preferences complete and full intake recorded.
No question, so full intake followed explanation.
rationales: This retains order, planned checking and missing intake.
Explanation and start times are reversed.
Preference check is planned; intake and condition are absent.
A dish-name question occurred; full intake cannot be inferred.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-257.reading:
Mealtime record
11:20: Staff explained the menu; the person asked one dish name again.
11:25: After the question was answered, eating began.
12:05: A post-meal preference check is planned. Intake and current condition are absent.
This record alone establishes neither full intake nor completed post-meal support.

options: November 9 usual reception; November 10 east entrance.
No advance consultation for difficult access.
November 9 east entrance, November 10 usual; consult before visiting if needed and check phone hours separately.
East entrance indefinitely and exact hours fixed here.
rationales: The dates are reversed.
Advance reception consultation is explicit.
This preserves period, consultation timing and separate hours.
Change ends the 9th and exact hours are absent.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-258.reading:
Visitor notice (fictional facility)
Reception change: From November 6 through 9, visiting reception is at the east entrance. Usual reception resumes November 10.
Contact: If the east entrance is difficult to use, consult reception before visiting.
Telephone: Call during opening hours, specified in a separate guide.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-259.prompt: What is required by October 2, and what follows?
options: Bring photos by then and display on family decision alone.
Contact the responsible worker; bring photos after confirmation and check personal wishes too.
No family-contact deadline is stated.
The same rules apply to every belonging.
rationales: The deadline concerns contact, with further conditions omitted.
This separates deadline, delivery and personal choice.
Family instructions explicitly state October 2 contact.
